source.inspection: Original PNG opened directly once, unmodified; no page image, modern candidate, crop, extraction, enlargement, OCR, or model used.
source.coordinateConvention: Approximate original-image pixel locations, origin upper left. Locations index observations only; they are not measurements, calibration, or approved construction coordinates.

composition.description: One monochrome perspective apparatus view: a tall framed, screw-driven, ribbed cylindrical assembly at left, a curved hose route between assemblies, and a circular pointer instrument on a branched base at right. There are no separate data panels, chart axes, or calibrated chart coordinates.

components.visible: An L-shaped bent arm rises at upper left, turns right, and meets a thick horizontal lobed handle or hub centered over the vertical screw. Black lobes and white breaks are visible.
ambiguities: The black hub merges with the arm and screw; exact attachment boundaries and hidden fastening geometry are unavailable.
White breaks cannot uniquely be classified as separate component edges rather than highlights.

components.visible: A central vertical, patterned screw-like section runs downward from the upper hub into a ring-shaped collar above the frame.
ambiguities: Individual upper thread turns are merged; an exact turn count is not uniquely recoverable.

components.visible: A perspective crossbar has a sloped rear/top edge and lower/front edge. A stacked oval collar surrounds the central screw. Small dark upright fastener-like projections appear near the left and right crossbar ends.
ambiguities: Exact collar layer count, fastener shapes, and screw passage boundaries are obscured by thick strokes.
No hidden underside joint may be reconstructed from the visible outline.

components.visible: A left vertical frame strip extends from the crossbar to the lower base. A right upright descends from the crossbar behind the hose and upper cylinder surface. The left strip overlaps the ruler-like area and cylinder edge.
ambiguities: The right upright is occluded at the hose and cylinder; its unseen continuation and attachment cannot be uniquely traced.
Left frame and ruler edges merge in places; the exact number of separate strips is not established.

components.visible: A vertical screw-like shaft below the crossbar has repeated diagonal or curved dark/light bands. It terminates visually at a small central fitting on the upper elliptical surface.
ambiguities: Thread turn count is not uniquely recoverable from merged strokes.
The shaft-to-fitting attachment has merged contours; no hidden piston or seal is visible.

components.visible: An elliptical top rim spans the left cylindrical assembly. The screw meets a small dark fitting near its center. A dark fitting or hose-associated shape is immediately to its right.
ambiguities: The screw fitting, hose-associated fitting, rim, and frame overlap; exact port and joint boundaries cannot be separated uniquely.
The image does not expose the interior, gas boundary, piston face, or sealing arrangement.

components.visible: The cylindrical wall contains a stack of curved, near-horizontal ribs or bands. They wrap toward the right edge and merge into darker outlines at the ends. The left frame masks their left portions.
ambiguities: The exact number of physical ribs versus outline, shading, and rim strokes is not uniquely recoverable.
Band spacing is perspective-distorted and supplies no approved volume or displacement scale.
No internal construction may be inferred from the ribbed exterior.

components.visible: A broad elliptical or rounded lower base surrounds the cylinder bottom, with dark lower edging and small foot or fastener projections.
ambiguities: Rim, cylinder-bottom, and shading strokes merge; exact layered-part and foot counts are unavailable.
Rear support details are not visible.

components.visible: A thick outlined hose-like route emerges visually near the left upper-surface fitting, rises in a large arch, curves right and downward, and forms a low bend beside the cylinder.
ambiguities: Its left endpoint merges with the upper fitting and rim; the exact connection point is obscured.
At the right side of the low loop, dark strokes meet the rightward route; crossing, overlap, and a continuous joint cannot be distinguished uniquely from pixels.
The hose interior and hidden joints are not visible.

components.visible: A thick curved route runs up and right from the left-loop region toward a horizontal fitting immediately left of the circular instrument's stem. Light breaks occur inside its dark outline.
ambiguities: Its merger with the left loop is dark and thick; exact topology is not independently visible throughout.
At the right termination, hose, collar, and stem outlines overlap; the hidden attachment is unavailable.
Light breaks are not evidence for additional valves or tube branches.

components.visible: One large approximately circular, perspective pointer-instrument housing has a thick dark outer ring, an inner light face, and a darker right/back edge. A neck below it meets the stem.
ambiguities: The exact front-ring and rear-housing boundaries merge at upper right.
Housing appearance does not establish pressure type, reference pressure, range, or unit.

components.visible: One prominent dark diagonal pointer-like stroke extends from a thick lower-left/central hub toward the upper-right portion of the face.
ambiguities: Hub, tail or counterweight, shaft, and pointer tip are not separately bounded everywhere.
The exact tip-to-tick correspondence and angular reading are not uniquely readable and are not approved.
No additional hidden pointer may be invented.

components.visible: A curved scale band follows the upper-left and upper arc and continues down the right/lower-right face. Short radial or rectangular marks of varying visible lengths are mixed with small numeral-like glyphs. Additional isolated small glyph or dot clusters occur on the left and lower interior.
ambiguities: Every individual tick cannot be separated from neighboring glyphs, borders, and merged ink; exact tick count and major/minor classification are unavailable.
The lower-right scale termination and overlapping marks are not uniquely bounded.
Small numeral-like glyphs are not reliably transcribable; no complete label set is recoverable.
Interior dots or glyphs cannot uniquely be identified as numerals, unit symbols, reference marks, or printing artifacts.
Exact tick angles, spacing, values, range, units, pointer reading, and reference-pressure convention remain unapproved.

components.visible: The dial has a short lower neck with curved collar strokes over a thick vertical stem. A horizontal hose-associated fitting is visible on its left. On its right is a collar or boss, a short outlined horizontal outlet-like projection, and a dark tip.
ambiguities: Exact internal connectivity, hidden passages, sealing joints, and valve functions are not visible.
The right-side projection's apparent end is visible, but whether it is capped, open, a control, or a connector is not established.
Collar counts and layer boundaries merge into the central dark stem.

components.visible: The stem meets a dark base with a broad branch extending lower right, a branch extending lower left, and a shorter rear/upper-left projection partly merged with the stem. Rounded dark ends are visible.
ambiguities: Three apparent projections are observable; this is not proof of the total physical leg count or hidden rear-leg layout.
Merged shading prevents unique recovery of all branch junction outlines and mounting fasteners.

labelsAndMarks.visible: One isolated uppercase B-shaped glyph next to the upper screw.
labelsAndMarks.transcriptionStatus: Shape recoverable; Latin B versus Cyrillic look-alike cannot be decided from the glyph alone.

labelsAndMarks.visible: One isolated italic L-like glyph to the left of the cylinder and scale strip.
labelsAndMarks.transcriptionStatus: Exact source character identity is unresolved from pixels alone.

labelsAndMarks.visible: One isolated uppercase M-shaped glyph to the right of the circular instrument.
labelsAndMarks.transcriptionStatus: Shape recoverable; Latin M versus Cyrillic look-alike cannot be decided from the glyph alone.

labelsAndMarks.visible: A narrow vertical ruler-like strip along the left frame/cylinder edge carries a descending series of short dark horizontal or slightly slanted marks, with longer or darker clusters near some levels. Upper and lower portions merge with the frame, rim, and base.
ambiguities: Individual ruler ticks cannot all be distinguished from overlapping support, rim, or shading strokes.
No unique mark count, full numeral transcription, origin, unit, end value, or ruler-to-volume mapping is available.
The cylinder-top/rim level near the strip is not an approved scale reading.

labelsAndMarks.visible: Small isolated black specks occur near and below the left base and hose. They are not treated as apparatus labels or measurement marks.
labelsAndMarks.ambiguity: Their cause is not identifiable from pixels; no meaning or geometry is assigned.

visibleConnections.visible: Upper arm/hub, upper shaft, central crossbar collar, and lower shaft align vertically.
Lower shaft terminates visually at a fitting on the upper elliptical cylinder surface.
Two upright regions bracket the central screw and overlap the cylinder/base view.
Hose loop meets the dark region near the upper cylinder fitting.
The low left hose loop and rightward hose route merge in the mid-right region.
Rightward hose meets the left side fitting of the instrument stem.
Dial, neck, vertical stem, and branched base form one vertically attached assembly.
A right collar/boss and short horizontal projection meet the central stem.

requiredAmbiguities: Complete dial tick set, individual tick count, and tick-versus-glyph distinction.
Complete dial glyph set and exact visible label transcription.
Complete ruler mark set and individual mark count at occluded/merged portions.
Hose loop merger topology and exact endpoint/joint boundaries.
Exact isolated left-label identity from pixels alone.
Thread/rib count and some obscured component boundaries.
uncertainty.geometryHoldReason: Independent source-pixel ambiguities remain in required marks, counts, labels, and connections. A qualitative draft would have to choose unsupported geometry or omit required source detail.
